# Chosen direction C — Seventies Sill

Seventies Sill presents Fernlight as a warm, slightly cheeky plant shop from 1974, redrawn with modern restraint. It speaks to the reader in their 20s to 40s with a crowded windowsill, who loves their plants as objects and wants a helper with personality, not a dashboard. The mood is sunny, tactile and reassuring. Terracotta clay, the colour of the pots themselves, owns the hero wall. A sharp new-leaf lime is the single accent, used for the second half of the headline, the primary button and one plant stake. Shrikhand, a fat retro display face, sets the headline at poster size with the confidence of a shop sign. Atkinson Hyperlegible keeps every sentence below it calm and very easy to read on a phone at night, so the weight contrast is both the joke and the clarity. The space is built around an object people will describe: an arched east window with a 70s sun rising inside it, and a full-bleed windowsill running edge to edge across the bottom of the hero. A snake plant, a Monstera and a cactus sit on the sill, each with a plant stake. Two stakes are blank; only the Monstera's is lit: Watering day, Thursday. That one image carries the promise: plants alive, and one quiet reminder. Below it, arch-topped cards with chunky offset shadows carry the proof points, and the care card is drawn as a punched plant label next to the worked sums. All the imagery is code-made SVG in a tight palette. The motion is a small sunrise: the sun lifts in the window, the three plants settle gently onto the sill one after another, and the Monstera's stake pops on last. It refuses pale green boxes, stock leaf photography, bubbly mascots, exclamation marks and nagging badges. It is playful in form and calm in voice.

Signature move: A full-bleed windowsill runs across the bottom of the hero under an arched east window with a 70s sunrise. Three plants sit on it, and only the Monstera's plant stake is lit: 'Watering day, Thursday'.
Motion: A small sunrise: the notice and masthead fade in, the two headline lines rise one after the other, then the subhead and buttons. The arched window fades in as the ringed sun lifts up inside it, the snake plant, Monstera and cactus settle onto the sill 150 ms apart with a soft bounce, the blank stakes fade in, and the lime Monstera stake pops up last. Everything animates from an offset to its natural state, inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
Imagery: A code-made SVG scene: an arched window with a cream frame and mullions, and a 70s sun inside it (a mustard disc ringed by clay and lime bands). Below it is a full-bleed sill, with a pale top face, a clay front edge and an ink shadow line, holding a flat-shaded snake plant, a Monstera with fenestrated leaves and a cactus, each in a different pot. HTML plant stakes stand in the pots: two short blank ones, and the Monstera's tall lime one, which rises clear of the leaves against the sun with 'Watering day / Thursday'. The care card in the second section is drawn as a punched plant label. There are no photos.
Direction notes: Art director's recommendation (benchmark run, not owner direction): In the renders, Seventies Sill is the page people would describe afterwards: plants alive on a real sill and one lit stake reading 'Watering day, Thursday', so the promise lands in one picture even at 390. Its warm, legible look suits a plant owner on a phone in the evening, and the care card and worked sums below show how the schedule is set.
